other_likely_causes: Damaged wiring harness or loose connector
Metallic debris buildup on the magnetic sensor tip
recommended_first_check: Remove the CKP sensor to inspect the magnetic tip for metallic debris and test sensor resistance/AC voltage output while cranking.
reasoning: The CKP sensor provides the critical engine position and timing reference needed for the ignition system to operate. A weak, shorted, or absent signal will prevent the ignition from firing properly, resulting in a no-start condition or engine stalling. These specific codes strongly point to a physical failure of the sensor itself or its immediate wiring circuit.
